subject: gk
question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): HDI can improve even with falling income levels.

Reason (R): Gains in health and education can compensate income loss.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both A and R are true, and R explains A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) measures a country's average achievements in three basic dimensions of human development: health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (gross national income per capita).
 
• HDI can improve even with falling income levels if there are significant improvements in other dimensions such as health and education.
 
• The Reason (R) that "Gains in health and education can compensate for income loss" directly explains the Assertion (A) that "HDI can improve even with falling income levels."
 
• For instance, countries with strong public health and education systems may see an increase in HDI rankings even if their income levels decline temporarily.
 
• This compensatory mechanism demonstrates the balanced structure of HDI, which does not solely rely on economic factors but incorporates human well-being comprehensively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A**

 
 
• This option is incorrect because Reason (R) directly explains Assertion (A).
 
• Without the compensatory mechanism of HDI (where health and education gains offset income loss), the assertion cannot hold true.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A is true, R is false**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because Reason (R) is a valid and accurate explanation of how HDI functions.
 
• Improvements in health and education are critical factors in HDI calculations and can indeed offset declines in income levels.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A is false, R is true**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the Assertion (A) is true. HDI can improve even with falling income levels due to gains in other dimensions such as health and education.
 
• While Reason (R) is true, it is not independent of Assertion (A) in this context.
 
 
 
• **About HDI:**
 
 
• HDI was introduced by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 1990 as a composite index to measure human development across nations.
 
• It is used to categorize countries into four tiers of human development: very high, high, medium, and low.
 
• The HDI aims to shift the focus of development economics from purely economic growth to human well-being.
